claims.text: NiTi shape memory alloy exhibits temperature-dependent plastic deformation behavior.
The temperature-dependent deformation behavior of NiTi is caused by its martensitic phase transformation.
NiTi is in the austenitic phase at higher temperature.
The high-temperature austenitic phase has a relatively ordered crystal structure.
Controlled cooling induces martensitic transformation in NiTi.
The experiments were conducted under well-controlled temperature gradients and consistent thermal cycling.
Martensitic-transformation microstructures form in NiTi upon cooling.
As temperature decreases, NiTi transforms from austenite to martensite.
The martensitic transformation facilitates deformation through reorientation and rearrangement of crystallographic variants.
Cooling NiTi through the onset of martensitic transformation increases its plastic deformation.
Austenitic NiTi is relatively stiffer than cooled, martensitic NiTi.
The room-temperature baseline is in the austenitic phase.
The extent of deformation is sensitive to NiTi alloy composition.
The extent of deformation is sensitive to processing history.
The extent of deformation is sensitive to thermal-cycling rate.
Sensitivity to composition, processing history, and cycling rate may limit generalizability.

contradictions.description: The conditions field states that experiments were conducted under controlled conditions, whereas the uncertainty field says system-specific experimental validation is still required and the falsification design describes those tests prospectively.
